Lingering

LING-ger-ing -- shares a root meaning 'long' with 'elongate.' · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Lingering is lasting for a long time, especially longer than expected; slow to end.

A lingering smell of smoke remained in the house long after the candles were put out.

Worked Example

Months after recovering from a bad cold, a runner notices she still gets unusually short of breath during workouts that used to feel easy.

That stubborn effect that refuses to fully go away, long after the original cause has passed, is exactly what lingering describes. Unlike 'brief,' which ends quickly, lingering implies something that overstays.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

persistent: continuing to exist or occur over a long period

enduring: lasting over a long period of time

prolonged: continuing for a longer time than expected

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

fleeting: lasting for a very short time

momentary: lasting only a moment

Where it sits · how actively it resists going away — enduring → lingering → persistent

enduring vs. lingering: Enduring can carry a more positive tone than lingering -- an enduring friendship sounds admirable, while a lingering symptom or smell usually sounds unwanted.

persistent vs. lingering: Persistent can feel slightly more active than lingering: lingering often describes something that simply hasn't faded yet, while persistent can suggest something that keeps recurring or resisting efforts to remove it.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — leng-

root — leng-: long (Old English/Germanic (lengen))

Put it together

Put it together: Linger comes from an Old English root related to 'long' -- to linger, at its root, means to make something last long, to stay longer than expected. Lingering describes exactly that overstaying quality.

Use the root in a new word: elongate

Use the root in a new word: elongate: The sculptor elongated the figure's limbs to make it appear taller and more graceful.
